3537.text: In Ps.40.14, Ps.70.2, Ps.71.13, and Ps.71.24 'seek' functions in the stock formulaic phrase 'those who seek my life/hurt' -- fully within the base gloss's hostile-pursuit sense, consistent across all four occurrences with no unique nuance.

3540.text: M07 (shame/disappointment, via H0954/H2659/H3637) is the fate wished upon those who 'seek' (H1245) the psalmist's life; the seeking (this cluster) is the malicious cause, and M07 is the desired consequence -- a cause-effect relational pairing across the verse.

4082.text: In 2 Kgs 1:3 darash names the illegitimate inquiry of Ahaziah's messengers to Baal-zebub, a pagan deity — the nuance here is negative/idolatrous consultation, contrasting sharply with the legitimate divine-inquiry sense (1 Kgs 14:5) and underscoring darash's capacity to name both true and false objects of seeking depending on context; the impact is rhetorical rebuke ('is there no God in Israel...') highlighting misdirected seeking.

4083.text: Other M-code tags present (M08/M74 arise, M37 meet) describe the messenger-angel's commissioning action and the encounter itself, not the inquiry-act; this cluster's vantage adds that darash here specifically names the illegitimate object of the seeking (Baal-zebub) which the arising/meeting sequence is sent to confront and correct.

4084.text: The operation 'inquire' is initiated by King Ahaziah (via his messengers, human party) and directed toward Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron (false-deity party) — a human-to-pagan-deity consultative movement that the Lord's angel is sent to rebuke.

4367.text: In 1Sam.9.3 'look' translates baqash in its plain concrete sense of searching for lost donkeys -- squarely within the base gloss 'seek' with no divergent nuance.

4373.text: In 1Sam.9.3 the operation 'look/seek' (role-T3) is initiated by the young man Saul is told to bring, directed toward the lost donkeys -- Kish's command sets Saul as initiator toward the object sought.

4377.text: 1Sam.9.3 contains no other M-code characteristic; H1245 (seek) stands alone in this verse's role annotations.

5313.text: 1Chr.22.19 'seek the Lord' is the classic devotional sense (1a3a), squarely within the base gloss.

5318.text: In 1Chr.22.19, darash (seek the Lord) sits alongside M47 (heart/mind, 'set your mind and heart to seek') and M44 (covenant, the ark of the covenant) -- the seeking here is explicitly heart-directed, showing darash functions as the outward enactment of an inward disposition (heart/mind) toward covenant faithfulness.

7073.text: Across this pass's 'inquire' surface-form cluster (1Kgs.22.8, 2Chr.18.7, 2Kgs.22.13/2Chr.34.21, 2Kgs.3.11, 2Kgs.1.2/1.3/1.6/1.16, 2Kgs.8.8, 1Kgs.14.5, Ezek.20.3, 1Sam.28.7, Jer.10.21, Gen.25.22, Exod.18.15, Deut.12.30, 1Sam.9.9, 1Kgs.22.7/2Chr.18.6, 2Kgs.22.18/2Chr.34.26, Isa.8.19, Jer.37.7, 2Chr.32.31, Isa.19.3, Zeph.1.6, Isa.11.10, Ezek.20.1, 1Chr.21.30, Isa.9.13) the term consistently denotes formal consultation of a deity or authoritative source (the Lord, a prophet, an oracle, Baal-zebub, mediums/necromancers) for a verdict or answer -- the single largest and most cohesive sense-cluster in H1875's full occurrence set, matching this subgroup's core description of institutional/cultic resort to authority for guidance.

7284.text: In 1Chr.22.19 and 2Chr.15.12 seeking is framed as a settled, wholehearted disposition ('set your mind and heart to seek', 'seek the Lord... with all their heart and with all their soul') rather than a transient emotional reaction -- the language of heart/soul signals an internalized, durable orientation.

7285.text: The felt quality of seeking varies by context: it is crisis-driven and emotionally anguished in Ps.77.2 and 2Chr.20.3 (trouble, fear), yet presented as a settled, wholehearted covenantal disposition in 1Chr.22.19, 2Chr.15.12, and 2Chr.22.9 ('sought the Lord with all his heart') -- the same term covers both transient emotional response and durable devotional orientation depending on narrative occasion.

7288.text: Seeking takes hold rightly under conditions of wholeheartedness and sincerity: 'set your mind and heart to seek' (1Chr.22.19), 'with all their heart and with all their soul' (2Chr.15.12), and freedom from co-present idolatry -- in Ezek.14.7 the presence of idols in the heart is what disqualifies otherwise-outward consultation. Genuine seeking requires an undivided heart free from rival objects of devotion.

7300.text: The evidence shows seeking engages the heart/soul level most deeply and consistently ('with all their heart and with all their soul', 2Chr.15.12; 'set your mind and heart', 1Chr.22.19), with the body's role limited to expressive gesture (Ps.77.2's stretched-out hand) rather than being the seat of the characteristic itself. The pattern indicates seeking's depth and seat is the heart/soul (volitional-affective center), while the body-link (where present) is expressive/indicative of the inner state rather than mediating or generative of it -- darash never engages purely bodily/instinctive levels without heart involvement in these texts.

7311.text: The pattern of engagement shows heart/soul faculties (mind, will, affection) consistently engaged when seeking is genuine (1Chr.22.19 'set your mind and heart', 2Chr.15.12 'with all their heart and with all their soul'), while purely external/ritual engagement without heart involvement is exposed as illegitimate (Ezek.14.3-7) -- indicating the characteristic's nature is fundamentally a volitional-relational act requiring the engagement of the inner faculties, not a mechanical or merely verbal performance.

7317.text: Adjacent characteristics appearing alongside seeking include 'heart/mind' (M47, frequently paired as the seat/manner of seeking, e.g. 1Chr.22.19, 2Chr.15.12, Ps.119.2/10), 'trust' (M19, Ps.9.10, Isa.31.1), and 'forsake' (M30/M59, as antithetical pairing, Ps.9.10, 1Chr.28.9) -- these co-occur with notable frequency, showing seeking is characteristically bound to heart-language and its antithesis, forsaking.

7323.text: Seeking is a constituent element of the larger characteristic of 'setting the heart' (2Chr.19.3, 2Chr.30.19, 1Chr.22.19 all pair 'set the heart/mind' with 'to seek') -- the heart-setting act supplies the internal disposition of which seeking is the outward-directed enactment, making seeking a component within the fuller act of wholehearted devotion.

12480.text: People select men for battle, leadership or a task, and the word marks fitness: "Moses chose able men out of all Israel and made them heads over the people" (Exo 18:25); "700 chosen men who were left-handed; every one could sling a stone at a hair and not miss" (Judg 20:16); "300,000 choice men, fit for war, able to handle spear and shield" (2Ch 25:5). The same word names the men "chosen from the assembly, well-known men" who rose up against Moses (Num 16:2).

12481.text: God chooses a person for a task or office: priests and Levites, the king, David, Solomon, the servant, witnesses. Choosing goes with bringing near: "The one whom he chooses he will bring near to him" (Num 16:5); "Blessed is the one you choose and bring near" (Psa 65:4). The choice is shown, not argued: "the staff of the man whom I choose shall sprout" (Num 17:5). It is followed by a charge: "the Lord has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary; be strong and do it" (1Ch 28:10). In the servant it is joined to God's soul and Spirit: "my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him" (Isa 42:1; Mat 12:18).

12483.text: God chooses a place "to make his name dwell there" (Deu 12:11), and the choosing carries his own presence: "My eyes and my heart will be there for all time" (2Ch 7:16). The people's offerings, eating, rejoicing, judgement, reading of the law and prayer are all directed to the place he chooses. The choice can be cast off, "I will cast off this city that I have chosen" (2Ki 23:27), and made again: "the Lord will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem" (Zec 1:17).

12487.text: Inner-being words stand beside choosing: God's heart in what he chooses, "My eyes and my heart will be there for all time" (2Ch 7:16); his soul in his chosen servant, "my chosen, in whom my soul delights" (Isa 42:1; Mat 12:18); the people's heart and soul turned toward the chosen city in repentance (1Ki 8:48; 2Ch 6:38); the soul's delight in chosen ways (Isa 66:3); the soul choosing death (Job 7:15); the heart given a worth (Pro 10:20); the soul's appetite, "whenever you desire" (Deu 12:21; Deu 18:6); the self humbled in a fast God does not choose (Isa 58:5); "one deeply despised" whom the Lord has chosen (Isa 49:7).

19627.text: 2 Samuel 6:16: "and she despised him in her heart": This verse was read for §2b from David's side. Here it is read for Michal.; *"As the ark of the Lord came into the city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out of the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the Lord, and she despised him in her heart"* (v16).; "Despised" is *bāzâ* (*to despise*; H0959), and it is *"in her heart"*. The contempt is inward first. It does not come out until David comes home to bless his household: *"How the king of Israel honored himself today, uncovering himself today before the eyes of his servants' female servants, as one of the vulgar fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!"* (v20).; Her measure is honour before others: *"honored himself"*, *"before the eyes of his servants' female servants"*. The joy she despises is joy *"before the Lord"* (v16).; David's answer brings in the choosing: *"It was before the Lord, who chose me above your father and above all his house"* (v21). The chapter names Michal *"the daughter of Saul"* three times (v16, v20, v23). I read the naming as setting her contempt in the house that was passed over. The text does not say this was her reason.; The same word, *bāzâ*, is the word in Isaiah 49:7, *"one deeply despised"*, set against the Lord's choosing (below).

19935.text: Carefulness, against presumption. When a case is *"too difficult for you"* (17:8), the decision is sought at the place. What is asked of the person then is *"you shall be careful to do according to all that they direct you"* (17:10), and not to turn *"to the right hand or to the left"* (17:11). Presumption is the opposite, and the man who acts presumptuously dies. The end is that *"all the people shall hear and fear and not act presumptuously again"* (17:13). I read this as a person's own judgement reaching its limit and being asked to yield. The passage gives the limit (*"too difficult for you"*) and the carefulness. It does not describe the inner struggle.

20305.text: Job 34:4 — Elihu: "Let us choose what is right; let us know among ourselves what is good": Elihu is angry with both sides. He *"burned with anger at Job because he justified himself rather than God"*, and at the friends *"because they had found no answer, although they had declared Job to be in the wrong"* (32:2–3).; He calls the listeners to weigh Job's case together, and calls that weighing a choosing: *"Hear my words, you wise men"* … *"for the ear tests words as the palate tastes food"*; *"Let us choose what is right; let us know among ourselves what is good"* (v2–4). The choosing here is not of a course of life. It is a judgement: picking out what is right in the case before them.; The picture is tasting. The ear tests (H0974) as the palate tastes (H2938). Then *"let us know among ourselves what is good"* uses the same words as Barzillai's *"Can I discern what is pleasant and what is not"* (2Sa 19:35): know (H3045), between (H0996), good (H2896). Barzillai said the palate's knowing had gone with age. Elihu uses the palate as the picture for weighing words.; What they are to weigh is Job's own claim. Elihu quotes it: *"I am in the right, and God has taken away my right"* (v5). He judges it at once: *"What man is like Job, who drinks up scoffing like water"*, *"who travels in company with evildoers"* (v7–8). His ground is God's justice: *"far be it from God that he should do wickedness"* (v10); *"his eyes are on the ways of a man, and he sees all his steps"* (v21).

20306.text: What this verse shows of choosing, as weighed by another: Weighing another person's choices is itself a choosing, *"what is right"*.; It is made together (*"let us … among ourselves"*), by testing words as the palate tests food.; It is a judgement on a case, not a course of life.; The one who calls for it has already decided (v7–8).

21298.text: Silent here is only the absence of voice in a thing or an enforced muteness and names no inner-being operation of the surface.

21309.text: Call is here a public proclamation, summons or announcement to others; it is the outward act and bears on the hearers, with no inner-being operation of the caller named.

21313.text: Called is here the outward act of summoning, addressing or sending for another person or thing; it bears on the other's response but names no inner-being operation of the one who calls.

21349.text: Deal here only handles, manages or settles a matter, a treaty or a plain term of dealing; no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

21408.text: Anger is here the anger, wrath, rage or fury of a person or people: a state of the heart aroused against another, a thing or God, named by the word itself.

21417.text: Fury is here the anger, wrath, rage or fury of a person or people: a state of the heart aroused against another, a thing or God, named by the word itself.

21468.text: Righteous here names an attribute of God or of his rule (a righteous Lord, the scepter of uprightness, the Holy One, his holy name or Spirit, the mystery of godliness); no operation of a person's inner being is voiced by it.

21503.text: Wicked is here the godly, the righteous, the upright, the wicked or the ungodly as a class of persons toward whom an act is directed or whom an event befalls (the Lord keeps the godly, do not envy the wicked, Christ died for the ungodly); the act is named by another word of the verse.

21515.text: Choose is here a person's own act of choosing or deciding: a purposeful act of the will that picks one thing, way, person or course over another (choose life, choose whom you will serve, decided in his heart, Mary has chosen the good portion).

21517.text: Choose here is God's choosing of a place, city, house or thing, or his own sovereign will over things (the place the Lord will choose, the city I have chosen, a body as he has chosen, the Lord is my chosen portion); no operation of a person's inner being is voiced by it.

21525.text: Chosen is here God's (or Christ's) own choosing of persons or a people (the Lord chose Israel, a chosen race, the apostles whom he chose, my chosen); it is his outward act upon them and bears on their standing and response, named by other words of the verse.
